b1b99c6174.q: Why is energy the critical bottleneck preventing data centers from solving enterprise AI?
b1b99c6174.a: Vedant explains that most data centers now have GPU capacity but lack the energy to run GPUs 24-7. Energy is fundamental because all AI depends on it—without solving the energy problem, you cannot solve the intelligence problem. This cascades: solving the GPU problem requires solving the data center problem, which requires solving the energy problem.
b1b99c6174.e: Disrupting Enterprise AI: Who Really Owns Your Intelligence? with Vedant Dwivedi
b1b99c6174.rq: Enterprise AI will be only successful when they will be holding the intelligence. If your intelligence is being held by any other company and that company depreciates the model over time, your intelligence moat is gone.

8fb77e2222.q: What is sovereign AI and why do enterprises need to own their intelligence instead of relying on external providers?
8fb77e2222.a: Sovereign AI means ownership of the entire energy layer and infrastructure where your intelligence lives. You must own all traces from data point, generation, monitoring, logging, and model creation. Enterprises cannot trust only five to six labs for all intelligence because intelligence capital—combined with human capital and money—forms the foundational pillar of enterprise growth, and outsourcing it entirely makes survival extremely difficult.

525f1525e3.q: What are the three main problems preventing enterprises from implementing AI successfully?
525f1525e3.a: First, enterprises are reluctant to share their data, yet without sharing data they cannot create good context for great results. Second, data is often too sensitive to share outside the organization—for law firms or pharma, the whole competitive moat is in the data. Third, even after sharing data with AI labs, enterprises don't get great results because there are no right tools and techniques, and the cost of sovereignty was previously extremely high.
